SEND
Our School
At Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School, we recognise that every child is unique.
We believe that every child should be given opportunities to succeed, within a safe, caring and stimulating environment, which should facilitate each child’s chance to reach the highest possible standards. Every child has full access to the entire curriculum during their schooling and teachers will make adjustments to their learning in order to allow every child to succeed.
All teachers strive to identify and address any barriers that are preventing children from making the progress they are capable of. All staff are committed to meeting the needs of all our children. As a school, we recognise the importance of not only supporting children’s academic progress but also developing their behavioural, emotional and social skills to enable them to become confident, independent learners and well equipped citizens for our society.
Our Parents and Further Support
We strive to maintain strong and productive links with parents and carers. We believe that good home school links and communication are essential to a child’s emotional well-being and progress.
If you are concerned that your child may have an additional need or are concerned about their academic progress your first point of contact should always be your child’s class teacher. Your child’s teacher will be able to direct you towards our SENCo if appropriate. Our school SENCo is Ms Carol Anderson. She can be contacted via senco@shirleywarren.co.uk or via the school office on 023 8077 3975
We understand that having a child with additional needs can be challenging. All the staff at Shirley Warren are here to help and want to make sure that you feel fully supported. You can speak to any member of staff to seek support.

Interventions
We offer a variety of other interventions at our school. These may be an academic intervention or an intervention to support a child’s emotional development. These may be run by either class teachers or teaching assistants. Where interventions require further training we may seek outside agencies to help us with this.
Our intervention programme is adaptable to our children and their needs. Parents will receive the opportunity to discuss these interventions with their class teacher at parent evenings.

Nursery
Click to enquire or enrol online
Our Early Years Vision
At Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School, we strive for children to be happy and confident learners. We believe that all children should have the opportunity to learn through play in a safe and stimulating learning environment, both inside and outdoors. Alongside this, children should be gently challenged and supported through positive adult interactions in order to develop their engagement, motivation and thinking skills. We value the importance of wellbeing and we endeavour to support our children in building resilience, learning to problem solve and becoming well rounded citizens. We have high expectations and aim to develop learning through creating real life experiences, a language rich environment and by offering children and families support when needed. We work as a team and in partnership with parents to plan high quality activities and provision which builds on children’s interest, wants and needs to develop their love of learning.
We are a diverse and inclusive setting and believe that every child has the right to high-quality early education and care and we are passionate about giving them exactly that.
________________________________________________________________________________
Our Setting
Our wonderful, well resourced Nursery welcomes children from 2 years old. Nursery is led by our Early Years Lead who is a qualified teacher. She also works closely with the Reception team to ensure the transition into school is a happy experience. Joining us at this early age, ensures that we get to know your children as they begin their journey at Shirley Warren and ensure your child has an excellent start to their educational life.
Children enjoy teacher led group activities, as well as free play, both inside and in the garden. Wet weather clothing is provided, so children have access to the outside all year round. Our skilled team support our children with individual next steps and capture the children's interests to make learning fun! We provide a healthy snack and drink (milk or water) during the session. You will need to bring a healthy packed lunch for your child.
We are also part of the Southampton Toothbrushing Scheme, where all children in Early Years brush their teeth every day (brushes and toothpaste are provided).

pageCache.pageTitle: Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School - Head's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head's Welcome
On behalf of the governors and our dedicated staff team, I am delighted to welcome you and your family to Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School. We are confident that your time with us will be positive, successful and full of opportunity.
I am proud to be the Acting Headteacher of Shirley Warren and at the heart of every decision I make is what is best for our pupils. Having worked at Shirley Warren for over ten years, I know our children, families and community well and I am deeply committed to ensuring that every child is supported to thrive- academically, socially and emotionally.
At Shirley Warren, we are committed to ensuring that each child is valued, cared for and given every opportunity to achieve their full potential. We aim to promote high standards of learning and behaviour through high-quality teaching and a broad, exciting curriculum that inspires curiosity, confidence and a love of learning. We believe in challenging and developing every pupil so that they leave us ready for the next stage of their education.
Everyone who visits our school comments on the warm and welcoming atmosphere. Our children are polite, friendly and proud of their school and there is a strong sense of purpose and belonging throughout our community.
Shirley Warren is a school that continues to grow and improve, driven by a shared commitment to providing the very best educational opportunities for our pupils. Parents and carers are an essential part of this journey and we recognise that children learn best when home and school work together. We warmly encourage families to engage with school life and be active partners in their child’s learning.
Our website is designed to provide you with useful information about our school. If you would like to discuss anything further, please do not hesitate to contact us using the details provided. We are always happy to help and are delighted to welcome visitors to Shirley Warren.
We look forward to working in partnership with you and your family and to supporting every child to flourish and succeed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School - Safeguarding
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
At Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School, safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is our highest priority. We are committed to ensuring that all pupils feel safe, secure and supported in school, at home and within the wider community.
All staff at our school have a shared responsibility to protect children from harm and to promote their personal safety, wellbeing, confidence and independence. We recognise our duty of care and will always take reasonable action to safeguard the welfare of our pupils.
If a member of staff has cause to be concerned that a child may be experiencing ill treatment, neglect or any form of abuse, the school will follow established child protection procedures and will work closely with Children’s Services and other relevant agencies where appropriate.
A clear Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy is available on the link on our Polices page and is reviewed annually by staff and the governing body. This is a policy adopted by the Bridge Trust.
If you have a concern that a child may be at risk of harm or if a child makes a disclosure (intentionally or unintentionally), please contact one of the Designated Safeguarding Leads as soon as possible.
Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs)
Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School has designated members of staff who oversee safeguarding and child protection across the school. The Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) who oversee safeguarding practice, monitor concerns and liaise with the local authority when necessary are:
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Sophia Ship, Acting Headteacher
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead(s): Matt Goodchild and Will Lyon, Assistant Headteachers and Rachel Head, Thrive Practitioner.
The DSL team monitors safeguarding practice, supports staff and liaises with the local authority when significant concerns arise.
If you are worried that a child is being harmed, is at risk of harm or if a child makes a disclosure (intentionally or unintentionally), please contact a member of the safeguarding team as quickly as possible.
If you are a young person, parent, carer or member of the public you can contact the Children’s Resource Service on 02380 83 3004 (Monday to Friday 8.30am to 5pm and Friday 8.30am to 4.30pm) or 023 8023 3344 (weekends, Bank Holidays and outside of office hours).
If you need to speak to a DSL regarding a safeguarding matter, please email the following email address: dsl@shirleywarren.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Shirley Warren Primary and Nursery School - PTA

PTA
As a parent or associate of the school, you are automatically a member of our Parent Teacher Association which we call SWIFT (Shirley Warren in Friends Together).
We orgnaise events for children and their families not only to give them enjoyable experiences but also to rasise money for school so that we can provide those little extras that school budgets do not allow.
Last academic year our Shirley Warren Wonder Bars were a roaring success with every child winning their own golden ticket prize. Our Summer Fayre was a fabulous event with a real family feel.
Monies raised this year have been put towards:-
~ a school tip for every year group
~ bouncy castle hire for the end of term
~ the purchase of a school BBQ
~ equipment and resources for the Summer Fayre
Our long term fundraising goal is to ensure the outdoor areas and playgrounds are well equipped and resourced.
If you would like to get involved in any way, please do let us know, we would love to hear from you!
SWIFT@shirleywarren.co.uk

Sports Premium
The government provides additional funding to improve provision of Physical Education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding is referred to as the Sports Premium and is provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport. The school can choose how we use the funding. The link below provides some guidance on how the funding should be spent.
Possible uses for the funding might include:
Hiring specialist PE teachers or qualified sports coaches to work with primary teachers when teaching PE
Paying for professional development opportunities for teachers in PE and sport
Providing cover to release primary teachers for professional development in PE and sport
Running sport competitions or increasing pupils’ participation in the School Games
Buying quality assured professional development modules or materials for PE and sport
Providing places for pupils on after school sports clubs and holiday clubs
